The Australian government has appointed former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock to review whether existing laws adequately protect freedom of religion.

The move aims to pre-empt a divisive fight over religious amendments to the same-sex marriage bill, though treasurer Scott Morrison insists the review cannot replace such amendments.

Prime minister Malcolm Turnbull says the review is necessary given the strong yes vote and imminent marriage equality legislation.

Coalition figures are split: some, like Peter Dutton and Mathias Cormann, back a separate religious freedom bill next year, while others, including Morrison and senator David Fawcett, want the issue addressed alongside the marriage bill. Ruddock is to report by 31 March.

Turnbull warns against broad, bill-of-rights-style measures that could cause uncertainty and unintended consequences, framing the review as a careful, expert stocktake. He says Ruddock is well-suited due to his experience as special envoy for human rights.
